proposal: The Mandate says the NSC should take a leading role in drafting and reviewing all formal national security strategies, that the NSC and OMB should prioritize White House review of the National Defense Strategy, review war plans and global force allocation with the Secretary of Defense, and review key Defense, State and Intelligence Community guidance before it is issued. It also says the NSC should rigorously review all general and flag officer promotions so that core military roles take priority over other matters.

status_summary: A new National Security Strategy was released on 2025-12-04 and a National Defense Strategy on 2026-01-23, but the public descriptions reviewed do not say that the NSC led their drafting or that the NSC and OMB reviewed the defense strategy, war plans or force allocation. On promotions, the White House acknowledged in July 2025 that the President personally meets candidates for four-star posts, which an Associated Press report described as a break from past practice; this is a White House review of the most senior nominees rather than an NSC review of all general and flag officer promotions. A Congressional Research Service product of 2026-07-17 describes promotion lists as going from the Secretary of Defense to the President and does not mention NSC review.

timeline.event: The White House acknowledged that the President meets with candidates nominated for four-star general and admiral posts, a practice the report said began at the Defense Secretary's initiative; the NSC is not mentioned.
The administration released its 2025 National Security Strategy.
The Department of War released the 2026 National Defense Strategy.

A CRS Insight on officer promotions described the statutory path of promotion lists (Secretary of Defense to the President) and congressional concern about personnel actions toward general and flag officers; it did not mention NSC review.

title: NSC to lead review of formal strategies, war plans and general and flag officer promotions
uncertainties: Not found: any report that the NSC itself reviews general and flag officer promotion lists; the presidential meetings cover four-star candidates only, and reported removals of officers from promotion lists were described as actions of the Defense Secretary, not the NSC. The public strategy summaries do not say who drafted them, and the 2026 National Defense Strategy document itself was not opened. Absence of public evidence is not evidence of absence, since NSC process is largely internal. The progress figure is an inference. Staffing is covered by c02-03 and cuts to general officer numbers by c04-09.
